overview: Pendennis Castle sits on the headland at the mouth of Falmouth’s harbour, a Tudor fortress built by Henry VIII to guard the coast. It has come through a long siege and two world wars, so there’s a lot of history packed into one place.

It’s a properly fun castle for families, run by English Heritage: ramparts to storm, tunnels to explore, big guns to look at, lawns for a picnic and sea views all round. With indoor and outdoor parts, it’s a good choice for a mixed day.

expect.title: The Tudor keep
expect.text: The round keep at the heart of the castle is around 450 years old and is the oldest part of the fortress.

expect.title: Ramparts, guns and tunnels
expect.text: Walk the ramparts, see the historic guns and head into tunnels that tell the castle’s wartime story.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: A small soft play area, a Castle Explorers trail and a build-your-own-city trail, plus volunteer-led tours with costumed characters from the past.

expect.title: Café
expect.text: The castle café has sea views.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry, free for English Heritage members. Booking online by midnight the day before is cheaper, and tickets are valid all day.

goodToKnow.label: Green travel discount
goodToKnow.text: Arrive by bus, train or bike and you get 20% off a ticket bought on the day: just show your travel ticket or helmet.

goodToKnow.label: Stay at the castle
goodToKnow.text: English Heritage has holiday cottages within the castle walls, if you fancy waking up on the ramparts.

week.text: Pendennis makes an easy family half day in Falmouth, rain or shine. Pair it with Falmouth’s town beaches and harbour, or take the ferry over to St Mawes, which has a castle of its own across the water.

pairWith.why: the maritime museum on the harbour
the headland viewpoint just beyond the castle

tips: Book online the day before for the cheaper ticket, unless you’re coming by bus, train or bike for the green discount on the day.
Bring a picnic for the lawns on a fine day.
